Why are we doing this?

Turn AI curiosity into the confidence to build

Vibe coding points toward a future of describing intent and building with AI. Companies are shaping it through assistants and agents. Learning to guide and verify their work matters more than learning another "magic prompt."

Why this workshop existsWhat you gain
Watching demos is not the same as buildingPractice changing, testing and explaining real software
Your experience deserves more than a static resumeA portfolio grounded in your own evidence
Useful AI needs more than a chat windowConnect UI, authentication, APIs and validated output
Faster output is not automatically trustworthyJudgment about facts, privacy, errors and quality

The goal is not to depend on AI. It is to become more capable with it.

Start: exercises/00-authentication.md. Keep the homepage public.

  1. Implement server-only configuration; reject missing/weak secrets
  2. Build signed four-hour sessions with Node crypto and random nonces
  3. Implement login/logout with HTTP-only, SameSite=Strict cookies; use Secure in production. Keep JSON/origin checks
  4. Guard layout and every private page, plus each private API
  5. Add classroom login throttling; test denial, expiry, tampering, logout

After build: logged-out pages redirect; private APIs return JSON 401. Missing configuration: 503. Valid tool requests: tool-specific 501.

Scope: one protected route, two validated modes, private UI state.

Interview

  • Do: true STAR evidence; mark unknowns and stages to confirm
  • Don't: invent stories, exact company processes or interview observations
Bad prompt, don't use: Build interview prep that invents leadership stories for me and predicts the exact company interview. Save everything to my public profile.

Study

  • Do: four weeks, measurable checks, each within weekly hours
  • Don't: guarantee a job or ignore the time budget
Bad prompt, don't use: Build a study planner that guarantees a job in four weeks. Ignore my available hours; accept any model response as a valid plan.

.github/workflows/pages.yml
name: Publish public portfolio
on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

  build:

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - run: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: out

The course repo is standalone, so the build runs from the repo root and uploads out.

  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

Push, inspect Actions, and open the deployed URL. No model key needed.
